scaffolding: Pure-Python stub of torch.nn, with only what the snippet touches: Module, LSTM, Linear and ReLU, exposed in the nn namespace.

Module registers each sublayer assigned as an attribute, by name, and raises AttributeError if the sublayer is assigned before Module.__init__, like real torch. So the super().__init__ of the snippet has an observable effect.

LSTM, Linear and ReLU store the configuration received, with the same parameter order and the same default values as real torch (LSTM: input_size, hidden_size, num_layers=1, bias=True, batch_first=False; Linear: in_features, out_features, bias=True; ReLU: inplace=False), so that positional or keyword calls give the same configuration.

LSTM validates like real torch (RNNBase.__init__, checked in github.com/pytorch/pytorch, torch/nn/modules/rnn.py): TypeError if hidden_size is not an int, ValueError if hidden_size <= 0, ValueError if num_layers <= 0.
Parameters with a default value in the stubs do not count in the Pysmell PAR, so the scaffolding does not trigger LPL.

run(dimensions): receives a dictionary with num_classes, input_size, hidden_size and num_layers, builds BasicLSTM and returns (hyperparameters stored in the model, configuration of each registered sublayer).
Checked: Pysmell only flags __init__ (PAR=5); nothing in the scaffolding.
pinned_behavior: typical: 27 classes, input 27, hidden 64, 2 layers; the model stores the 4 dimensions and registers lstm (27, 64, 2 layers, bias, batch_first), fc_1 (64 -> 32), fc_2 (32 -> 27) and relu.
edge: all dimensions equal to 1, the smallest valid ones; fc_1 keeps its fixed 32 outputs.
invalid: hidden size zero raises ValueError (it comes from the LSTM).
not_pinned_on_purpose: Order in which the sublayers are registered: it changes the order of the state_dict keys, but not its content or how it is loaded.
Message of the ValueError: it comes from the stub, not from the snippet; the test only pins the type.
Identity of the layer objects: the test checks the configuration, not the concrete class.
notes: The names of the sublayers (lstm, fc_1, fc_2, relu) and the 4 hyperparameters are pinned because they are public attributes of the model: the sublayers become the keys of the state_dict, which the original main() saves to disk (torch.save(ltsm.state_dict(), ...), line 199), and fwd uses num_layers and hidden_size.
